chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

A man comes to me seeking goods for ten thousand dirhams, or less or more, and I have only goods worth one thousand dirhams. So I borrow from my neighbor and take from this one and that one, then I sell them to him. Then I buy them from him (or instruct someone to buy them) so I return them to their owners. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods you don't fully own by borrowing from others to complete the sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the permissibility of 'bay' al-ma'dum' (selling what is not in possession) through a practical mechanism of borrowing goods to fulfill a specific contract, a view supported by many Shia jurists as distinct from the stricter prohibition of selling non-existent items. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates this method, highlighting the flexibility in commercial transactions when the seller acts in good faith to deliver the exact goods promised, thereby avoiding the uncertainty (gharar) associated with pure speculation.
